blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Deployment keeps identical Pods running. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: When its Pod template changes, the Deployment replaces the Pods. This lesson controls how.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Deployment, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name with kubectl rollout to watch and undo updates.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web

blocks.title: Four copies and their label
blocks.what: Keep four Pods running, and manage the Pods labelled app: rolling-web.
blocks.why: Four copies make it easy to watch Pods being replaced a few at a time.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Four copies of the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rolling-web

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. Changing it starts an update.
blocks.why: Any change under template, such as an image or a variable, makes new Pods.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rolling-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rolling-web

blocks.title: A page that shows its version
blocks.what: busybox writes a page saying version, then serves it on port 80.
blocks.why: Reading the page shows which version a Pod runs.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: A small web server that shows its version
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rolling-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rolling-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]

blocks.title: The version number
blocks.what: VERSION is 1, and the command writes it into the page. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: Changing VERSION changes the template, so it starts a rolling update.
blocks.ifRemoved: The page says just version, with no number.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rolling-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rolling-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
          env:
            - name: VERSION
              value: "1"

blocks.title: Ready before traffic
blocks.what: A readiness probe asks each Pod for its page, as in the probes lesson.
blocks.why: A rolling update waits for each new Pod to be ready before removing an old one.
blocks.ifRemoved: New Pods count as ready the moment they start, even if the server is not yet answering.
blocks.comment: Count a Pod as ready once its page answers
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rolling-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rolling-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
          env:
            - name: VERSION
              value: "1"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 80

blocks.title: Replace a few at a time
blocks.what: RollingUpdate swaps Pods gradually. maxSurge allows one extra Pod; maxUnavailable: 0 keeps all four serving.
blocks.why: The app never drops below four ready Pods during an update.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses the defaults: a rolling update with 25% surge and 25% unavailable.
blocks.comment: Add one new Pod at a time, and never drop below four ready
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rolling-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rolling-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rolling-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
          env:
            - name: VERSION
              value: "1"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 80

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Deployments are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the Deployment.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running: four.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is rolling-web.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: rolling-web, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Write a page saying version and $VERSION, then serve it on port 80.
notes.spec.strategy: How the Deployment replaces old Pods with new ones when the template changes.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].na: VERSION, which the command writes into the page.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].va: Version 1. Quotes keep the number as text, as env values must be.
notes.spec.strategy.type: RollingUpdate, the default: replace old Pods a few at a time.
notes.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate: Limits on how many Pods change at once.
notes.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge: At most one Pod above replicas during an update: five in total.
notes.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailab: Zero: never fewer than four ready Pods during an update.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].readines: Checks the Pod can serve its page before it counts as ready.
Check by asking for a web page. Any status from 200 to 399 passes.
The port busybox’s web server listens on: 80.

tryIt.result: Prints successfully rolled out once all four Pods are ready.
Changes the template, which starts the update. In real work, edit the file and apply it instead.
Counts the new Pods: 1, 2, 3 out of 4 new replicas updated, then successfully rolled out.
Events show the new set growing by one while the old set shrinks by one, in turns.

questions.question: During an update, what is the most Pods that can exist at once?
questions.explain: replicas is 4 and maxSurge allows one extra, so five at most.

questions.question: Why does maxUnavailable: 0 matter?
answers: The update never drops below four ready Pods
The update happens all at once
questions.explain: An old Pod is removed only after a new one is ready, so capacity never dips.

questions.question: Which change starts a rolling update?
questions.explain: Only template changes make new Pods. Changing replicas just adds or removes Pods.

fix.message: The Deployment "rolling-web" is invalid: spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: Invalid value: 0: may not be 0 when `maxSurge` is 0
fix.explain: With no extra Pods and none allowed down, the update could never replace a single Pod.
